## L1 Capability: Data Security

Data Security is the enterprise security capability that establishes and governs the protection of data assets throughout their entire lifecycle — from creation, classification, and storage through processing, transmission, sharing, and destruction. As the architectural protection plane for the enterprise data estate, Data Security is a cross-cutting capability consumed by every application, platform, and infrastructure domain that handles sensitive or regulated information. It interfaces with Identity and Access Management (to enforce data access decisions based on verified identity), Network Security (to protect data in transit at the network layer), Cloud and Infrastructure Security (to ensure platform-level data protection controls are architecturally sound), and Security Operations (to detect and respond to data-centric threats). Data Security provides data-centric protection as a shared architectural concern — ensuring that sensitive data remains protected regardless of where it resides or flows across the enterprise.

## L2 Capability Areas

| L2 Capability | Description | Maturity |
|---|---|---|
| **Data Classification and Cataloging** | Identification, labeling, and inventory of data assets by sensitivity tier, regulatory classification (PHI, PII, CUI), and business value — establishing the classification schema that all other Data Security capabilities consume to make protection decisions | Developing |
| **Encryption** | Protection of data at rest, in transit, and in use through cryptographic mechanisms — ensuring data remains unintelligible to unauthorized parties regardless of the storage or transport medium | Developing |
| **Key and Secrets Management** | Lifecycle governance of cryptographic keys, certificates, secrets, and tokens — including generation, distribution, rotation, storage, revocation, and destruction — ensuring that cryptographic material is managed with the same rigor as the data it protects | Developing |
| **Data Loss Prevention** | Detection and prevention of unauthorized exfiltration, leakage, or mishandling of sensitive data across endpoint, network, cloud, and application channels — enforcing data handling policies at the point of egress | Initial |
| **Data Masking and Tokenization** | Obfuscation techniques applied to sensitive data in non-production, analytics, and integration contexts — enabling data utility while preventing exposure of original sensitive values | Initial |
| **Post-Quantum Cryptography** | Architectural readiness and migration framework for quantum-resistant cryptographic algorithms — ensuring long-lived cryptographic protections remain viable against emerging quantum computing threats | Developing |
| **Data Access Governance** | Policy-based control over who accesses what data, under what conditions, and subject to what approval and review lifecycle — enforcing minimal data exposure through entitlement management and access review | Initial |
| **Data Privacy and Residency** | Architectural controls ensuring data handling aligns with privacy obligations and geographic or jurisdictional constraints — governing where data may be stored, processed, or transmitted | Initial |
| **Secure Data Lifecycle Management** | Governance of data retention, archival, dormancy, and secure destruction in alignment with legal hold, business requirements, and regulatory obligations | Initial |
| **Data Integrity and Non-Repudiation** | Mechanisms ensuring data authenticity, tamper evidence, and audit accountability — enabling detection of unauthorized modification and providing cryptographic proof of data origin and chain of custody | Initial |

## Scope and Boundaries

**In Scope**: Protection of data assets at all sensitivity tiers across cloud, hybrid, and on-premises environments; cryptographic protection, classification, access governance, loss prevention, and lifecycle management as architectural outcomes

**Out of Scope**: Data management strategy and data quality (Information domain); security operations response to data breaches (SecOps domain — `strategy/guidance/security/SecOps/`); identity lifecycle management for data consumers (IAM domain — `strategy/guidance/security/Identity/`); network-layer traffic encryption beyond data-centric cryptographic controls (Network Security domain)

**Non-ABB Guardrail**: This document defines capabilities at L1/L2 only. Architecture Building Blocks, solution patterns, security controls, vendor selections, and compliance requirements are explicitly out of scope for this artifact.
